description: Typed current result families that an artifacts/** description asserts as registered while current-result-registry.json carries no result_kinds[] row for them. The gate tools/artifact_lint:asserted_result_families_are_registered refuses any such name that is not listed here, so this file is the visible ledger of assertions that outran the registry. It is a ratchet: entries may only be removed, and a listed family that becomes registered is itself an error.
adjudication: Opened 2026-09-19 with the gate. chris adjudicated on 2026-09-19 that artifacts/** descriptions are a normative surface, which is what makes an assertion here a registration claim rather than commentary. Seven names were asserted and none was registered. did_core_id was not a family at all -- the sentence meant that organization_id is a did_core_id -- and was rewritten to name the family it actually intends. mimi_room_binding and moderation_franking_proof were registered in the same batch because their subject and their value were both fully determined by the payload schema. The four below are not deletable and not mechanically derivable: each needs one design decision that the descriptions do not contain, so each is listed with the exact missing decision rather than guessed at. Do not add an entry to defer work that is derivable. Reviewed again on 2026-09-19 by reading the whole spec rather than the descriptions alone. Two of the four reasons below were wrong and are replaced: the recorded blocker had been dissolved by prose that the entry never consulted, and in both cases a different, sharper blocker was found in its place. Correcting a reason is not adding or removing a name, so the ratchet still holds: the set of listed families may only shrink.

unregistered_families.reason: The subject is settled and is no longer the blocker: models/event-and-patch.md section 4.2.4 says the two spellings land in two INDEPENDENT typed current results of the object_redaction family, that they never merge, and that a reducer MUST NOT canonicalize the ak:event: spelling into the derived object's typed id. So the two writers are not required to produce one subject; they contribute disjoint subjects in one subject space, the canonical typed-id string, and each row names its own carrier (payload.message_id for ak.message.redact, payload.target_ref for ak.redaction). What blocks registration is the value: the only member neither writer duplicates elsewhere is preserve[], whose items are a bare array of unconstrained strings with no field-path grammar anywhere in zh/**, no statement of what a second redaction of an already-redacted subject does to it, and therefore no way to say whether the projection is a replacing set or a monotonically shrinking intersection. Give preserve[] a defined item grammar and a repeat-redaction rule in models/event-and-patch.md first; the registry row follows mechanically from that.

ak.policy.rule asserts subject rule_id, but rule_id matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ and tools/identifier-classification-registry.json classifies it as a document_local_symbol -- resolvable only inside the containing object and never an authorization subject. policy_rule_state_payload carries no policy_id, so the same rule_id asserted against two different Policies would collide on one subject. Separately, models/governance-objects.md section 3.2 makes rules a required non-empty array inside the Policy object and defines the whole priority / default_effect evaluation over that array, so a free-standing rule has no policy_kind, no scope and no default_effect and cannot be evaluated on its own. Registering this family needs governance-objects.md to say whether ak.policy.rule addresses a slot of a named Policy -- which means the payload gains policy_id and the subject becomes the (policy_id, rule_id) pair -- or whether the rule set is only ever written whole by ak.policy.set. That is a change to the Policy write surface, not a registry edit. The earlier reason recorded here, that there is no append projection kind, no longer applies: models/common-fields.md section on the keyed-set join settles that an append-shaped family is keyed_set_add with the canonical event dot as its tag, and the append-only sentence that prompted it has been removed from the payload description because a typed current result has one current value and one revision per selector.

ak.view.reconcile asserts subject view_id and value = the whole View definition. models/views.md section 3.2 gives a second registered projection over the same subject under the family name view, written by ak.view.create and ak.view.update, and that name is not registered either. Registering view_reconcile alone would put two families on one view_id whose writers disagree about which is current; registering one family needs models/views.md to say whether reconcile replaces the same family's value or is a separate one, which the description does not say. Decide the family count first, then register both in one batch.

ak.organization.discovery asserts subject organization_id and a closed state value, and its payload def is the sibling of organization_moderation_policy_state_payload, which asserts the same shape in words this gate cannot see. The two should be registered together so the Organization surface does not acquire one registered family and one unregistered one, and that pairing needs the Organization state surface settled in governance/content-moderation.md rather than one row added here.
